title: Find a Safe Walk Through a Grid
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix grid and an initial health, determine if you can move from the top-left to the bottom-right corner while maintaining a health of at least 1, avoiding cells that reduce health.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix grid and an initial health, determine if you can move from the top-left to the bottom-right corner while maintaining a health of at least 1, avoiding cells that reduce health.
constraints: grid is a nonempty binary matrix with at least two and at most 2,500 cells.
Start at the upper-left and move in four directions; each unsafe 1 cell entered, including the start, costs one health.
Return whether the lower-right is reachable while final health remains at least one.
hints: Maximizing remaining health is equivalent to minimizing the number of unsafe cells visited.
Run Dijkstra on the grid with cell values as entry costs.
Initialize with the starting-cell cost, relax four-neighbor costs, and require minimum loss < health.
All weights are nonnegative, so Dijkstra finds minimum loss; positive final health is exactly the strict inequality.

tests.explanation: A path of only safe zero cells reaches the destination without losing health.
Every path costs at least three health, leaving zero, so the result is false.
